metadata.title: Why the Best AI Detector Might Never Ship.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: why is the AI detector I can use so bad? Lands the carry-out that the failure is structural, not a motive.
metadata.anchor_pair: S03 -> S13 (must be the SAME composition)
metadata.one_flag: S11 — reported figures; S12 removes the argument's dependence on them
metadata.sensitivity: Adjacent to a named company's motives. No motive is asserted anywhere. See SCRIPT.md 'Deliberately not claimed'.

beats.narration_text: Someone asked why AI detectors stay bad when the companies say they could do better. The answer is structural. Liam. Take them through it.

shot.new_visual_element: Shannon puppet, lab, speaks to camera, hands off

beats.note: Audio baked into media/B00.mp4 by Seedance (voice MARCUS). No mp3 for this beat.

beats.narration_text: The company required to build AI detection is the same company that loses if the detection works well.

production_viz.label: One entity, two labels
production_viz.mechanic: A single shape on cream carrying two labels at once: BUILDS IT on one edge, PAYS FOR IT on the other. One object, not two.

beats.narration_text: That's not an accusation. It's the shape of the arrangement, and it doesn't change no matter who's running the company.

production_viz.label: The shape survives the people
production_viz.mechanic: The S01 shape held fixed. Behind it, a series of anonymous silhouettes swap through. The shape never moves.

beats.narration_text: Hold on to something odd: nearly every colour printer made in the last few decades secretly prints tiny yellow dots that identify it.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — the yellow dot grid

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — the yellow dot grid
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A printed page on cream; a magnifier reveals a faint grid of yellow dots. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT S13.

beats.narration_text: The obvious read here is that a company had a good detector, buried it, and dressed the burial in excuses.

production_viz.label: The cover-up reading
production_viz.mechanic: A working tool locked into a drawer; a press release taped across the front. Sell the cover-up reading as reasonable.

beats.narration_text: But look at the excuses: paraphrasing really does strip these marks, and false positives really do land hardest on people writing in a second language.

shot.new_visual_element: The objections, shown to be real

production_viz.label: The objections, shown to be real
production_viz.mechanic: Two panels, each showing the objection actually happening: marked text paraphrased until the mark is gone; a clean second-language passage flagged in error. Both are real failures, drawn straight.

beats.narration_text: Those aren't flimsy reasons. They're the reasons a careful person would give — which is exactly what makes the story hard to read from outside.

production_viz.label: Sound reasons; no verdict
production_viz.mechanic: Both objections stand, unstruck. Where a verdict stamp would go, a single terracotta question mark. Nothing is refuted.

beats.narration_text: Here's the structure. Someone wants detection to exist — a regulator, a school, a court.

production_viz.label: Someone asks for detection
production_viz.mechanic: Three asking parties on one side, a single labelled requirement rising between them.

beats.narration_text: The only party who can build it is the one whose product it makes less attractive.

shot.new_visual_element: It lands on the party it costs

production_viz.label: It lands on the party it costs
production_viz.mechanic: The requirement travels across the frame and lands on the S01 shape — the party it costs. No one else can receive it.

beats.narration_text: And whoever ships it first is punished for it, because users can move to a competitor that hasn't.

production_viz.label: First mover is punished
production_viz.mechanic: One provider ships a marked product; a stream of users flows out of it toward an unmarked rival. The mover shrinks.

beats.narration_text: So even a company that wants to ship a strong detector has a reason to wait for everyone else.

production_viz.label: Everyone waits
production_viz.mechanic: Four providers, each holding a finished detector, all watching each other. Nobody steps forward.

beats.narration_text: One flag — the specific figures here, an accuracy number and a share of users who said they'd leave, come from press reporting on internal documents, not from anything published for checking.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ONE FLAG — reported, not published

production_viz.label: THE ONE FLAG — reported, not published
production_viz.mechanic: Two figures rendered inside a dotted border, captioned 'reported, not published'. A single terracotta FLAG marker over the beat — the reel's only hedge, labelled as one.

beats.narration_text: But the incentive doesn't depend on those numbers being right; it's there at any size.

production_viz.label: Numbers gone; shape remains
production_viz.mechanic: The dotted figures fade out entirely. The S01 shape remains, unchanged and unlabelled by any number.

beats.narration_text: Which brings back the printers: that worked because every manufacturer had to do it at once, so nobody lost anything by being first.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — every maker, dotted

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — every maker, dotted
production_viz.mechanic: THE S03 COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical — same page, same magnifier, same dot grid. Then the frame widens: a row of pages from different makers, every one dotted.

beats.narration_text: The dots survived for decades not because printer companies were more honest, but because none of them could defect.

production_viz.label: No defector slot
production_viz.mechanic: The row of dotted pages held. One slot at the end is empty and outlined — the defector position, with nobody standing in it.

beats.narration_text: So a weak detector doesn't prove anyone chose weakness — the technical problems are real and unsolved.

shot.new_visual_element: Weak, and nobody proven to have chosen it

production_viz.label: Weak, and nobody proven to have chosen it
production_viz.mechanic: WEAK DETECTOR at the top; an arrow to the conclusion 'SOMEONE CHOSE THIS' — struck through terracotta.

beats.narration_text: And a company naming those real problems doesn't prove weakness wasn't chosen — both can be true at once, and from outside you can't separate them.

shot.new_visual_element: Real reasons, and still no answer

production_viz.label: Real reasons, and still no answer
production_viz.mechanic: Mirroring S15: 'THE REASONS ARE REAL' at the top; an arrow to 'SO NOTHING WAS CHOSEN' — struck through. Both struck conclusions now sit side by side.

beats.narration_text: You don't need bad faith. You just need the same company to build the detector and pay for it working.

props.quote: You don't need bad faith. You just need the same company to build the detector and pay for it working.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Find a case where the party required to measure a problem is the party the measurement costs — emissions self-reporting, safety incident logs, a platform's own moderation numbers. Write down who would lose if the measurement got sharper, and what would have to be true for them to sharpen it anyway. The pattern isn't about AI, and once you can name it you start seeing it where nobody has ever suggested wrongdoing. Liam, in for Bear.
